units: <cite ref="Berakhot 15a:2">Ber. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>מעלה … והקריב עליו ק׳</he> it is accredited to him, as if he had built an altar and offered a sacrifice on it; <cite ref="Sukkah 45a:7">Succ. 45ᵃ</cite>. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. II, Par. 2 <he>כל מקום שנאמר ק׳ אמור ביו״ד ה״א</he> wherever in the Scriptures ‘sacrifice’ is used in connection with the divine name, the latter is written with Yod He (<he>יהוה</he>, never <cite ref="A01789"><he>אלהים</he></cite>).
Ned. I, 4 האומר ק׳ … שאני וכ׳ if one making a vow says, ḳorban … that I will (not) eat &c.
Ib. II, 5 בק׳ וכ׳ (נדר) if a man in making a vow uses the word ḳorban, and then says, I vowed only by the gifts to kings; a. fr.—Pl. קָרְבָּנוֹת.
<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 14:10">Zeb. XIV, 10</cite> <he>קָרְבְּנוֹת הצבור</he> congregational sacrifices, <he>ק׳ היחיד</he> sacrifices offered by individuals.

<cite ref="Taanit 27b:5">Taan. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>כבר תקנתי להם סדר ק׳ וכ׳</he> I have arranged the order of sacrifices for them (in the Torah), and when they read these sections, I will account it to them as if they offered them.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 30:13">Ex. R. s. 30</cite> <he>בקש הקב״ה … ועבודת ק׳ וכ׳</he> the Lord wanted to give them (the generation of the flood) four things (to purify them), the Law, sufferings, the sacrificial service, and prayer, but they refused; a. fr.
